title: Creating Zipper Bottom Stopper
content: **Zipper Structure![ziper_structure.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775849506841)** **Bottom Stopper** ※ Please check the requirements and recommendations for the Bottom stopper below. **[Required]** * The Bottom stopper(zipper) file format must be *ZSP or *ZST. * The Bottom(Open) Stopper is produced with two OBJs, while the Bottom(Closed) Stopper is produced with a single OBJ. * The OBJ should only contain the Stopper Mesh. * When registering the zipper file, it will be all created in size #3 (100%). Please create the stopper file(OBJ) in size #3. * The mesh’s normal direction must be facing outwards. * Align the MESH position according to the purpose of each axis. X-axis | Place the point where the zipper tape touches each stopper at the X-axis 0. ---|--- Y-axis | Top Stopper Position the point of the top stopper that aligns with the endpoint of the zipper tape at the Y-axis 0. Bottom Stopper Position the point of the bottom stopper that aligns with the bottom of the slider at the Y-axis 0. Z-axis | Place the slider's zipper tape faces at the Z-axis 0. * In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status **[Recommended]** * If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. * If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. * For the complex graphic pattern, please use the Normal map. **(e.g. logo, pattern, etc.)** * The scanned OBJ is compatible, but the mesh should be re-meshed and editable. * It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. **Open Bottom Stopper** * From the Front View, the origin (0,0,0) is the bottom part where the slider can be all the way down. Therefore, place the stopper where it touches the slide at the origin. ![1.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775817715609) * From the Top View, the zipper teeth are placed on the X-axis of 0. Place the zipper teeth of a stopper on the X-axis of 0. ![2.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775800660889) ![3.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775859736345) <The position of each Open Bottom Stopper Mesh on the Grid> **Closed Bottom Stopper** * From the Front View, the origin (0,0,0) is the bottom part where the slider can be all the way down. Therefore, place the stopper where it touches the slide at the origin. ![4.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775859960857) * From the Top View, the zipper teeth are placed on the X-axis of 0. Place the zipper teeth of a slider on the X-axis of 0. ![5.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775866972185) ![6.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775801237657) <The position of each Closed Bottom Stopper Mesh on the Grid> **1\. Bottom Stopper Registration** **1\. Open 'CLO S/W'** **2\. Open 'Register OBJ'** from the Main menu > Material > Zipper > Register OBJ ![7.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775801507225) **▶Basic** * **Type****:** Stopper / Select Bottom(Open) or Bottom(Closed). * **Name****:** Enter the name of the file to be created. * **Scale****:** Select the same scale unit when creating the OBJ. * ****Axis Conversion :** Set the axis to ensure the Stopper's proper placement.** **▶File**** ** * **OBJ** : Import the OBJ file to be registered. * Bottom(Open) Stopper - The first loaded OBJ will be positioned in the direction of the zipper generated first. **▶Preview** : Check the imported Stopper file in advance. **▶OK/Cancel :** Click OK to finish the file creation when the file registration is done. _**The created file is saved in each object folder as**Assets > Materials > Hardware_and_Trims > Zipper.****_ **2\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the ZSP to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775867549465) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory) ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** Please provide the default size of the ZSP that you created for customers. title: Creating Button
content: **Objective ** Create Button items by using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** ** ****[Required]** * The mesh’s normal direction should be facing outwards. * The point where the OBJ button will be anchored to the garment must be placed at the origin (0,0,0). * In the Description, the following product information must be provided. (1) Vertex Counts (2) UV MAP unwrapping status **[Recommended]** * Button OBJs should be made with less than 10,000 triangles, so there is no speed problem in CLO software simulation. * UVs should be unwrapped to prevent overlapping, enabling users to apply a variety of textures without issues. * In the case of a button with a thread, the thread mesh must be named 'Ren_Thread' to separate the button and thread from the CLO software Material. (**To create BTN file by THREAD TYPE** for reference) * If the mesh and the normal map share the same position and direction, it may lead to overlapping and flickering issues during rendering. Make sure to avoid overlapping the mesh. * If two or more vertices are located in the same place, please weld them together. * please use the Normal map for the complex graphic pattern. **(e.g. logo, pattern, etc.)** * It is recommended to use textures with a maximum size of 512 pixels. * The scanned data is compatible, but the mesh should be meshed and editable. * It is recommended to add an edge loop(s) to define the sharp edge. **1\. title: Step 4: FAQ
content: ### **📋****Basic Questions** **Question: Where can I find the VRChat avatar/clothing/accessory creation guide?** Answer: <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/> **Question: How do I install Modular Avatar?** Answer: Please refer to the official Modular Avatar documentation: <https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/> **Question: Where can I download Unity and VRChat SDK?** Answer: * Unity Hub: <https://unity.com/download> * VRChat Creator Companion (VCC): <https://vcc.docs.vrchat.com/> **Question: Must I use Unity version 2022.3.22f1?** Answer: Use a Unity version compatible with VRChat SDK 3.5.2+. The latest version can be confirmed in the official VRChat documentation. 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/sdk/upgrade/current-unity-version/> **Question: Can I use a different workflow?** Answer: Yes, but you must provide a detailed guide for buyers. **Requirements:** * Step-by-step installation method * Include screenshots * FAQ and troubleshooting methods * * * ### **🔧 Unity Package Related** **Question: What if my Unity Package exceeds 1GB?** Answer: Adjust texture resolution or remove unnecessary files. Main methods: * Reduce texture resolution (2048→1024) * Delete unused Blendshapes * Remove hidden polygons * Optimize materials **Question: Should I check 'Include dependencies' when exporting Unity Package?** Answer: Yes, you must check it. If unchecked, necessary Shaders or Materials may be missing. * * * ### **📊 Polygon & Performance Rank** **Question: What is the recommended polygon count for VRChat avatars?** Answer: * **PC:** 70,000 triangles or less (Good Rank standard) * **Quest:** 20,000 triangles or less (required) ⚠️ Exceeding 70,000 triangles will drop the rating to 'Very Poor'. 💡Related Documentation * **Performance Ranks (Official Documentation)** 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/> * **Avatar Optimization Tips (Official Documentation)** 🔗 <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-optimizing-tips/> **Question: If Performance Rank is 'Very Poor', can I still sell it?** Answer: Yes, sales are permitted. It is common for popular avatars across various marketplaces to have a 'Very Poor' rating. While CONNECT does not impose restrictions based on Performance Rank, please note that buyers may prefer optimized avatars. **Question: Where can I check polygon count?** Answer: In Unity, check at `VRChat SDK Control Panel → Avatar Stats`. * * * ### **🎨 Shader & Material** **Question: My avatar/clothing displays in pink.** Answer: Shader is missing. Solution: 1. Import required Shaders (lilToon, Poiyomi, etc.) **before** importing Unity Package 2. If Shader is already installed, reassign the Material **Question: My avatar/clothing displays in white.** Answer: Material is not applied. Solution: 1. Find the Material and assign it to the avatar's Mesh Renderer 2. Or drag and drop the Material directly onto the avatar part * * * ### **💨 PhysBone Related** **Question: PhysBone doesn't work in-game.** Answer: Please check the following: 1. Verify VRChat SDK is the latest version (update via VRChat Creator Companion) 2. Verify PhysBone component is assigned to the correct bone 3. Recheck after test upload to VRChat **Question: PhysBone Transform Count error occurs.** Answer: Too many PhysBones. Solution: 1. Delete unnecessary PhysBones 2. Add End Bone to 'Ignore Transforms' 3. PhysBone count limits: * PC: No limit (but consider performance) * Quest: Maximum 8 PhysBone components, 64 affected transforms **Question: Cannot set PhysBone on End Bone.** Answer: Error occurs if the end bone is branched. Solution: * Add endpoint bone using Endpoint Position * * * ### **📤 Upload & Sales** **Question: How do I test upload to VRChat?** Answer: In Unity: `VRChat SDK → Show Control Panel → Build & Test` **Question: What files should I include in Unity Package?** Answer: * **Required:** Prefab, FBX, Textures, Materials, etc. - files used in item creation * **Recommended:** ReadMe.txt, usage guide * **Optional:** .blend, .psd (source files)

title: Step 2: Production Workflow
content: The VRChat item creation process follows the recommended workflow for CONNECT sales. For guidance on the basic creation process, please refer to the official VRChat guides below. **VRChat Official Guides** 🔗**VRChat Creators Main:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/> 🔗**VRChat Avatar Guide:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/> 🔗**Creating Your First Avatar:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/creating-your-first-avatar/> **VRChat Performance Rank Reference** We recommend creating items with the total polygon count (avatar body + clothing + accessories, etc.) according to the following platform-specific standards: * **PC - Good Rank Recommended Standard** : Total polygon count of 70,000 triangles or less * Quest compatibility: Total polygon count of 20,000 triangles or less 🔗**Performance Ranks:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-performance-ranking-system/> 🔗**Avatar Optimization Tips:** <https://creators.vrchat.com/avatars/avatar-optimizing-tips/> 🔗**Android Content Optimization (Quest):** <https://creators.vrchat.com/platforms/android/quest-content-optimization/> * * * Below are the essential and recommended settings for each item type: ### **2-1. Avatar Creation** **Essential Settings** * **Humanoid Rig Setup** * **Add VRC Avatar Descriptor Component** * View Position Setup (viewpoint position in VRChat - recommended between both eyes) * Avatar Size **(Humanoid standard)** : 0.5~5m (average 1.65m) * Exceeding this range may cause IK operation errors in VRChat. **Recommended Settings** * **Eye Bone:** For eye movement simulation * **Viseme:** Recommended for mouth shape setup (Blendshape method recommended) * **PhysBone:** For physics effects on hair/tail, etc. * **Blendshape:** For facial expressions and appearance changes * Please optimize the avatar's polygon count so buyers can combine various clothing/accessories. ### **2-2. Clothing Creation** **Essential Information** * **Specify Compatible Avatar** * Please clearly indicate the avatar name(s) that the clothing is compatible with in the description so buyers can confirm (e.g., Lucy) * We recommend including the avatar's sales link for easy buyer verification. * **Specify Clothing Polygon Count** * Please list the total polygon count of the clothing in the description so buyers can confirm. * Use Triangle standard for specification (e.g., +8,500 Triangles) * We recommend minimizing polygons so buyers can combine with other items. **Recommended Settings** * **PhysBone Setup** * We recommend adding PhysBone to parts that need movement, such as skirts or capes, to add swaying effects. * Excessive PhysBone can cause performance degradation, so please use only where necessary. * For Quest compatibility, we recommend minimizing PhysBone usage. * **Penetration Prevention** * Please minimize clothing clipping through the avatar's body. * Pay special attention to arms, chest, and thigh areas as they have significant movement, and we recommend testing with various body types and poses. * **Remove Unnecessary Polygons** * Please delete hidden avatar body parts under clothing (e.g., torso and arms not visible when wearing a top). * Removing internal clothing faces and invisible details will reduce unnecessary polygons and improve performance. * **Quest Optimization** * For Quest platform compatibility, we recommend consolidating Materials into one. ### **2-3. Accessory Creation** **Essential Information** * **Specify Compatible Avatar** * Please clearly indicate the avatar name(s) that the accessory is compatible with in the description so buyers can confirm (e.g., Lucy) * We recommend including the avatar's sales link for easy buyer verification. * **Specify Accessory Polygon Count** * Please list the total polygon count of the accessory in the description so buyers can confirm. * Use Triangle standard for specification (e.g., +3,200 Triangles) * We recommend minimizing polygons so buyers can combine with other items. * **Specify Attachment Location** * Please specify where the accessory attaches (e.g., Head, Hand, Back, Chest, etc.) **Recommended Settings** * **PhysBone Setup** * We recommend adding PhysBone to parts that need movement, such as earrings or tail accessories, to add swaying effects. * Excessive PhysBone can cause performance degradation, so please use only where necessary. * For Quest compatibility, we recommend minimizing PhysBone usage. * **Attachment Location Considerations** * **Head:** Please position so it doesn't obstruct vision. Especially earrings, hats, etc. need verification from first-person perspective. * **Hand:** Please configure to accurately match hand bone positions. Testing is needed to ensure natural appearance during hand movements. * **Back** : Please verify no clipping through avatar body or floor when sitting or lying down. * **Chest:** We recommend allowing tolerance to accommodate chest size variations. * **Consider Multiple Accessory Combinations** * Since buyers often wear multiple accessories simultaneously, please minimize individual accessory polygons and Materials. * For example, we recommend creating each accessory lightweight so earrings, necklaces, bracelets, bags, etc. can be worn together. * **Quest Optimization** * For Quest platform compatibility, we recommend consolidating Materials into one. * * * ### **📦 Unity Package Export** After completing production, create a Unity Package. **Export Steps:** 1. Select the folder/files to upload in the Project window 2. Top menu: `Assets` → `Export Package...` 1. **Required Check:** ☑️ `Include dependencies` 3. Select save path and click save button **Notes:** * **Maximum file capacity: 1GB** * Verify all essential assets are included (Prefab, Textures, Materials, Meshes, etc.) * Do not include SDK or Modular Avatar itself (buyers install separately) **Reference:** [Unity Package Official Guide](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/AssetPackages.html) * * * ### **✅ CONNECT Recommended Production Method** CONNECT recommends the following production method to enable buyers to use items easily and quickly: **1\. Provide as Unity Package** * `.unitypackage` format * Maximum capacity: 1GB * Include all assets (Prefab, Textures, Materials, Meshes, etc.) **2\. Include Prefab** * Provide in Prefab format so buyers can use it immediately by dragging and dropping onto the avatar * Reference: [Unity Prefab Guide](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/Prefabs.html) **3\. Modular Avatar Compatible Structure** * **Rigged Items** (clothing, long tails, wings, etc.): * Must include bone structure * Bone names must match the target avatar * Mesh must be properly skinned * **Non-Rigged Accessories** (hats, glasses, etc.): * Provide in Prefab format positioned appropriately for easy buyer placement For details: [Modular Avatar Official Documentation](https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/docs/intro), [Clothing Compatibility Guide](https://modular-avatar.nadena.dev/docs/tutorials/clothing) **4\. Include Basic Information in Item Description** * Compatible avatar list * Simple installation/usage instructions (e.g., "Apply using Modular Avatar") * Required tools (Unity version, VRChat SDK, Modular Avatar, etc.) * * * ### **⚠️ If Using a Different Production Method** If using a different method than the recommended production method above, please **specify the usage guide in the Description** for buyers: **Recommended Inclusions:** * Basic installation method * Compatible avatar list * Required tools/assets (e.g., specific Shader, VRCFury, etc.) * FAQ (optional) **Providing a detailed guide is optional but recommended:** * Step-by-step installation method (including screenshots) * Format: PDF, Notion/Google Docs link, or ReadMe.txt

title: Creating 3D Garment
content: **Objective** Create Garment content using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. **Required & Recommended** When creating and uploading a Garment file, please follow the rules below. **[Required]** * The garment file format must be *zprj, *zpac. * The garment should be simulated on your avatar (including hangers). * The garment file may include an official CLO/Marvelous Designer avatar or an avatar with an authorized resale license when you upload an item in the Garment Category. * The sewing lines should not be twisted. * Collision issues between layers should be resolved if you are designing a layered garment. * It is not possible to delete/add/replace the Trim and Fabric files after Publish. * It is not possible to add, delete, or replace different Design Sources after Publish, for garments that include Design Sources. * The majority of the components should consist of 2D patterns produced by pattern-making in CLO or Marvelous Designer software. * The 2D pattern should have a reasonable particle distance. The recommended particle distance value is 5 to 20. * 2D patterns should be arranged as neatly as possible in the center. Avoid overlapping patterns in the 2D Pattern window. * 2D patterns that are the same pieces(e.g. Jackets, Pants, etc.) should be close to each other and should be easily recognized as one piece. * The unnecessary notches and baselines inside the 2D pattern should be deleted before publishing. **[Recommended]** * The garment should have Fitting Suit information for compatibility with the Auto Fitting function. * The garment should be saved after deactivating the Strengthen, Freeze feature. * You have to save the garment after simulating it in the A pose or the T pose. * A collision between trims should be resolved if trim category items (e.g., Buttons, Zippers, Hardware, Fasteners, Notions) are added to the garment. **Details** **1\. Loading Avatar** \- Use the default avatar from the software. Library ▶ Avatar \- Use a customized Avatar from the software. Main Menu ▶File ▶ Open ▶ Avatar **※Fitting Suit** \- CLO Software Users CLO's default avatar is wearing a Fitting Suit. Fitting Suit is a device that helps the CLO's Auto Grading function to work. If both avatars have Fitting Suit information when wearing the same 3D costume to different size avatars, they can be draped to the appropriate size for each avatar without any special pattern modification. If the outfit uploaded by the Seller is a ZPAC file using the CLO default avatar, the Auto Grading feature makes it easier for buyers to use 3D costumes. \- Marvelous Designer Software Users The Marvelous Designer default avatar is also wearing a Fitting Suit. You can also add Fitting Suit information to your avatar if you are using the Marvelous Designer software version 10 or higher. Please refer to the [link](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2NjCNZxcYtk&t=77s) for detailed instructions. **2\. Creating Patterns / Sewing / Simulation** * Create patterns using the pattern generation tool from the 2D window. * Sew patterns created by using the sewing tool from the 3D or 2D window. * When sewing is completed, press the simulation button to simulate the costume on the avatar. **※Particle distance** For smooth operation speed, we recommend working at the default value of 20. When submitting the final costume file, make sure that the particle spacing is set as a reasonable value. By default, 5 is recommended, and 3 is recommended if the pattern is small. **※Layer** When creating a costume with multiple layers, it must collide between layers. You can set the order of layers by setting the layer value from the simulation properties pane. It is recommended to change the value to zero after the simulation is complete. ![Property_Editor.jpeg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775564555673) **3\. Setting up textures** From the Properties Editor, you can add/modify textures that are used for garments. ![Property_Editor_2.jpeg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775531859865) **4\. Saving Files** Save the garment file according to the specified file format. \- ZPAC Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Garment If you save it through the above path, the only garment except the avatar is automatically saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as ZPAC. \- ZPRJ Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save as ▶ Project If you save it through the above path, the garment including the avatar is saved. In this case, the file extension is saved as .zprj. ※Note: Only ZPAC or ZPRJ files can be uploaded in the Garment category. **5\. Creating Render Image** Allows all 3D Window screenshots or images rendered by other software. **6\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the GARMENT to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775532040729) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory) ** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (**Mandatory**)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3\. DESCRIPTION ** If you are selling a physical product, please provide the sales page URL in the description. When you enter the URL with 'http://' or 'https://,' the link will be generated automatically. **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the Garment. However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the Garment. If you are selling a physical product, it is also acceptable to upload actual photos. **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register an image that well showcases the characteristics of the Garment. If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please register the rendered image. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.

title: Convert to Game-Ready Asset using Everywear
content:
Before getting into EveryWear, please take the time to check the information below. * [**What is EveryWear?**](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304312078873-What-is-EveryWear) * [**Preparing and Starting EveryWear**](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304285349273-Preparing-and-Starting-EveryWear) * [**Garment Tab**](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301912857-Garment-Tab) * [**Material Tab**](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302920217-Material-Tab) * * * ### **1\. Optimizing the Garment’s Poly Counts** Please optimize the polygon count of the garments to make sure that the created outfit runs without any issues. To optimize the garments' polygon counts, you have several options: **you can adjust the pattern's particle distance value or use EveryWear's 'Polygon Optimization' feature.** Please optimize your outfit with the most convenient option, but not exceed the maximum poly counts listed below. After optimizing the polygon count of the pattern, please also optimize the polygon count of accessories such as buttons, zippers, and trims. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088457497)
```
✔️Double-check if the patterns have been changed to ‘Quad (Optimized).
``` **[Optimize the garment with the ‘Polygon Optimization’ feature]** 1. Open EveryWear * From the main Menu → CONNECT → Open ‘EveryWear.’ 2. Enter the appropriate polygon count in the ‘**Garment Polygons** ’ tab of the Garment tab. 3. Click ‘Optimize.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088462233) 4. Simulate the optimized outfit. ``` 💡Note: How to Adjust Polygon Count for Accessories like Buttons, Zippers, and Trims Using the Optimize function in Polygon Optimization, accessories such as buttons, zippers, and trims may be converted to billboards (planes) during the polygon optimization process. In this case, you can adjust the polygon count for each accessory separately from the patterns by changing the Billboard setting to Mesh in the Property Editor for the respective accessory. Then, enter your preferred value to control the polygon count.
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51683960687001)
```
For buttons or trims that are prominently noticeable, it's recommended to use ‘Mesh’ instead of ‘Billboard’ types. During Polygon Optimization, buttons or trims might be converted to billboards, so it’s advisable to choose the appropriate ‘Mesh Type’ based on the situation.
``` * * * ### **2\. Sealing Openings with Auto Seal** Use the **Auto Seal** function to create capping faces over any openings where the garment’s interior might be exposed—such as hems or sleeve cuffs. This prevents the inside of the garment from showing even when the avatar moves, resulting in a higher‑quality finish. Hidden inner faces are also automatically masked, ensuring that unnecessary internal geometry is not rendered, which improves overall optimization. 1. In the **Garment** tab, open **Polygon Optimization** and click **Auto Seal** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088463897) 2. Create a guide line. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510088472217) * **Disk Mode:** In the 3D viewport, click three points on the pattern to generate a disc; the curve formed where the disc intersects the pattern becomes the guide line. * **3D Pen Mode:** Draw a curve directly on the garment (same as the existing 3D Pen tool). Note that the first and last points must meet for the curve to be created. 3. Select the Auto Seal direction. * Using the guide line, choose which side of the new Auto‑Seal face will be exposed. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51682161663001) * In this garment’s case, the sealed face should be oriented downward, so click when the lower portion is highlighted. ``` 💡Auto Seal – Before and After Comparison Image
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510133038489)
```
⚠️ To view the surface generated by Auto Seal in the 3D window, the following two settings must be enabled:
1. 3D Window > Garment Rendering Style > Thick
2. Select Pattern > Geometry > Extrusion Direction > Back Face enabled
If the surface is not visible after using the Auto Seal function, please check that both of the above options are correctly set.
``` * * * ### **3\. Polygon Masking for Hidden Garments** Utilize the ‘**Masking Brush** ’ for additional optimization, such as inner pocket linings or areas hidden by the avatar. For more details, please check the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301912857-Garment-Tab)]. 1. Click the brush icon in the ‘**Polygon Optimization** ’ section under the Garment Tab. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510211598617) 2. Select the appropriate settings in the ‘Masking Brush’ option and use the brush to specify the masking area. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510230841241) * * * ### **4\. Rigging Clothing** Rig the optimized garments to the template avatar’s joints. 1. Click ‘**Apply** ’ in the Rigging option of the EveryWear. (Do not use **Max Influence Joints.**) ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510230842265) ```
⚠️ The ‘Max Influence Joints’ option specifies the maximum number of joints affecting each vertex. The number on the right indicates the ‘Max Influence Joints’ value of the imported avatar. This option is recommended for use only when the ‘Max Influence Joints’ value for the rigged garment needs to be set differently from that of the imported avatar.
```
```
📢 All rigging data will be deleted if you change the design or run a simulation. Therefore, please make sure to rig with the final design.
``` * * * ### **5\. Modifying the Skin Weight of the Clothing** Once rigging is done, click the brush icon to adjust the skin weight and silhouette of the garments. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510279058585) Please refer to the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301912857-Garment-Tab)] or check the [[Tutorial](https://youtu.be/wKjp2Xo0VCQ?si=DDSAWi7oqUpkXg90&t=343)] for more detailed instructions on the brush's weight and sculpt tabs. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510279065497) * * * ### **6\. Applying Skinning Test Motion and Checking the Rigging Quality** To check the garments have been rigged accurately, please apply rigging test motion files to check any areas that require adjustment. 1. From the main menu, File → Open → click ‘Joint Motion.’ 2. Import the motion file (.mtn). 3. From the main menu, select **Animation → Animation Editor**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669010585) 4. Slide the ‘Frame Bar’ to check if the garments follow the avatar’s motions appropriately. * Please return to the Skin Weight step to address necessary corrections if adjustments are required. 5. Apply the ‘A-pose’ file after the rigging process is completed. ``` 💡Key areas for Skin Weight Adjustments💡
``` * Collar![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621570073) * Armpit![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669018137) * Pants![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669020057) * Skirt![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621579929) * Wrist & Ankle![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669022745)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669025945) * Elbow & Knee![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621584665)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669031193) * * * ### **7\. UV Packing** The ' UV Packing ' feature automatically aligns the UVs of the garments. Please refer to the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302920217-Material-Tab)] for more details. 1. Click the ‘**Material Tab** ’ in EveryWear. 2. In the UV Packing section, set the ‘**Image Size(Pixels)** ’ to 2048 and the ‘**Seam Size(Pixels)** ’ to 8. 3. Click ‘**Pack UVs.** ’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621594009) 4. In the ‘**Option** ’ section, set the packing options as shown in the image below. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510621600665) 5. Selecting **‘0 to 1(Default)’** in the ‘UV Area’ section to generate a single UV map. 6. Click the **‘Apply’** button. ```
⚠️ Please refer to the [[Document](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302920217-Material-Tab)]to understand the purpose of each ‘UV Packing’ option and select the appropriate settings based on your needs.
``` * * * ### **8\. Texture Baking** Create the ‘**Detailed Normal Map** ’ and **‘Ambient Occlusion Map** ’ based on the suited outfit. 1. Check the ‘**Detail Normal Map** ’ and ‘**Ambient Occlusion Map** ’ under the ‘Texture Baking’ Section. 2. Click ‘**Apply**.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669038745) 3. Click the ‘**Preview** ’ button to check the generated maps. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51683771227545) ```
💡Note: When the back side of a pattern is facing outward, please use the ‘Flip Normal’ function to toggle between the front and back sides of the pattern as needed. During the ‘Texture Baking’ step, set the outward areas to the front side of the pattern to generate correct shading on the ‘Ambient Occlusion Map’ and proceed with baking. While uploading the FBX, please use the ‘Flip Normal’ function to set the back side of the pattern facing outward as required.
```
```
▶ Differences in the ‘Ambient Occlusion Map’ results depend on the front/back side settings of the collar pattern.

```
▶ Differences in stitch lines depend on the pattern
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510669043609) * * * ### **9\. Changing Avatar Pose to Default Pose** Change the avatar's pose by applying the Default pose. 1. Go to **File → Open → Pose** 2. Select the ‘**inZOI_DefaultPose.pos’** file that matches the gender of your avatar 3. Click ‘**Open’** **Please make sure to select the options shown in the image below when opening the pose file.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51510671165977)

Go to the [**Gamewear**](https://connect.clo-set.com/gamewear/inzoi) page located at the top of the main screen. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722342448409) 1-2. Select the desired outfit and click the **Download** button. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722372258713) 1-3. Once the download is completed, you may be able to find the file that is automatically saved to the **[Downloads]** folder. ### **2\. Extract the ZIP File** 2-1. ```
⚠️ When extracted into the ‘Mods’ folder, you may find a created folder named in the format ‘ModName_UniqueID.’
The internal structure of the folder is as follows.
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51721992815641)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51721956219033)
```
⚠️ ‘LucyCha’ in the sample path above (C:\Users\LucyCha\Documents\inZOI\Mods) represents your User Account Name. Please replace it with your actual OS (Windows/Mac) user name. How to check your ‘User Account Name
▶ Window
1. Press `Window key + R` to open ‘Run’ dialog.
2. Type `cmd` and press Enter.
3. In the command window, type the following command: `echo %USERNAME%` ▶ Mac OS
1. Search `Terminal` in `Spotlight(⌘ + Space)`
2. In the Terminal window, type `echo $USER` and press Enter.
``` 2-3. Please check that a folder has been created in the Mods directory after extraction. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722135660185) ### **3\. Applying Outfit in the Game.** 3-1. Launch the game. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722132571673) 3-2. Click ‘Character Studio. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722135663769) 3-3. In the bottom menu, select the ‘Outfit’ category. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722132573593) 3-4. Go to the ‘Set’ tab, then click on the downloaded ‘Mods’ outfit to apply it. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51722132574233)
```
⚠️ Essential Notes - Please make sure the game is fully closed when installing ‘Mods’ file.
- If you can’t find the ‘Mods’ file in the game after installation, try restart the game.
- The game will not recognize the outfit unless the file is extracted to the ‘Mods’ folder.
``` * * * ### ### **💡When Mods Don't Show Up (How to Fix Disabled Mods)** If you're experiencing any of these issues, your mods may be disabled: ❌ Installed 'Mods (custom-outfits, furniture, etc.)' are not showing up in the game. ❌ 'Mods' stopped working after the game update. **Why Do Mods Get Disabled?** inZOI automatically disables all mods when the game is updated to ensure stability. > 📢 Official Notice: "For game stability, all mods will be automatically disabled when updates or patches are applied."

Go to `Documents\inZOI\mods\[mod name] `folder 2. Open `mod_manifest.json` with a text editor 3. Find `"bEnable": false`, and change it to `"bEnable": true,` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/54054978861849) 4. Save the file **Method 2: Use Mod Browser (88849 Folder)** * Move your mods to `Documents\inZOI\mods\88849` folder * 'Mods (custom items)' will be automatically detected within the game's '**Mods** ' menu. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/54054994213529)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/54054994214937) **Method 3: Unofficial Mods (**[**Mod Enabler**](https://www.nexusmods.com/inzoi/mods/1)**Users Only)** 1. Go to `Steam installation folder\steamapps\common\inZOI\BlueClient\Content\Paks\[mods folder]` 2. Change `.pak_disabled` extension to `.pak`

title: Create Clothing
content:
Design the clothing that suits the game. Check the availability of the clothing before you start the design. * **Available Clothing Types** * Top + Bottom * Top + Bottom + Outerwear ```
⚠️ You do not create the following items: Hats, Socks (including ‘Leg warmer’), Shoes.
``` * * * ### ### **1\. Create Clothing** 1. Import the desired avatar (.avte) 2. Create the clothing to fit the avatar. * All trims on the garment should be attached using the Glue function. ```
💡Check the following guidelines when creating clothing
``` * To maximize the use of polygons, it’s recommended to delete the hidden parts of the clothing, especially when clothing has multiple layers and heavy linings. *Example) Pocket linings, the parts of the clothing obscured by layering, etc * ![Delete mesh_ref.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505335332505) * ![Delete mesh_ref2.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351024281) * ![Delete mesh_ref3.png](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351026585) * When creating skirts, make them within the guidelines indicated on the avatar for fitting stability. * ![이미지 022.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351028377) * The length of the sleeve should not intrude below the guideline indicated on the avatar’s hand. * ![이미지 020.jpg](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505351032089) * When creating the pants, the length of the pants should not touch the ground. * Must use the provided template shoes ONLY for the CONNECT. ### ### **2\. Garment Simulation** Apply all the garments to the template avatar and simulate them for stabilization. If the value ‘**Add’l Thickness - Collision (mm)** ’ is lower than the default value of **2.5mm** , the collision between garments during simulation may become unstable. Therefore, it is strongly recommended to set the value of ‘**Add’l Thickness - Collision (mm)** ’ to **2.5mm** or higher before the simulation. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505537924889) ### ### **3\. Modifying all patterns to Quad-Type** 1. Select all patterns (Ctrl+A). 2. Change the mesh type (Mesh Style) in the Property Editor to **Quad(Optimized**). ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505553523865)
```
⚠️ Please avoid using the ‘Quad (Grid)’ option in the Mesh Type (Mesh Style).
``` ### **4\. Modifying Top Stitch Type** Please change the type of the top stitches used in the garment to ‘**Texture type**.’ 1. Click the ‘**Topstitch** ’ tab in the Object Browser. 2. Select all Stitches. 3. Change the stitch type to ‘**Texture** ’ in the Property Editor. ```
⚠️ Please note that the Custom TopStitch currently provided by CONNECT does not support Texture type, so it cannot be used in EveryWear.
``` ### ### ### **5\. Modifying the thickness properties of the garment** The thickness type of the garment affects the polygon counts, so it should be defined before beginning the optimization process. If you are creating the thick type of garment, please change the ‘Garment Rendering Style’ mode to ‘**Thick Textured Surface (Alt+1)**.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505875616537) **Setting Thickness Properties** The pattern thickness property can be set in the Geometry option of the pattern’s Property Editor. For more details on **Geometry properties** , please check the [Documentation](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358238232985-Add-Pattern-Thickness). **How to Set Thickness Property** 1. Select the pattern for which you want to adjust the thickness property. 2. After selecting the pattern, go to **Property → Geometry → Add’l Thickness - Rendering (mm)** and change the value to **3**. It’s recommended to use a value of **1–3** to make the garment thickness appear slightly exaggerated compared to real clothing. You may adjust this to be thinner or thicker depending on the material or specific case. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505875619097) 3. Select the **Extrusion Direction** and whether to generate each side of the pattern. If the **Extrusion Direction** is set to “Forward” or “Both,” the thickness will be added outward, which can make the garment’s silhouette appear larger. Therefore, **please set all patterns to “Backward” by default** when working. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51505842884249)
``` 💡 In some cases, it may be necessary to keep the visible outer surface while deleting the invisible inner surface to optimize it. In this case, you can optimize by maintaining the Front Face option checked (status: On) and unchecking (status: Off) the Back Face option. How to use : 1. Select all patterns (Ctrl+A).
2. Property Editor → Check off the Back Face option in the Geometry section.
3. Select the patterns for which you can see the inner surface.
4. Check the Back Face option (status: On).
``` 4\. Set the side surface properties of the pattern using the Side Geometry option. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51508838744985) The Curvature (%) and Resolution settings under Side Geometry control the curvature and segmentation of the pattern’s side surfaces. A higher Resolution value results in more detailed segmentation, while a lower value maintains a flatter shape. (Setting the value to 0 disables the side surface entirely.) Since this setting directly affects optimization, we recommend setting the Resolution to 2 or higher only when segmentation is necessary for the pattern’s side.
``` 💡 Comparison of Side Geometry Based on Curvature (%) and Resolution Values
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51508819940249) ### **6\. Applying Fabric Materials** Apply appropriate fabric materials that match the garment design. You can either use fabric presets (`*.zfab`) available in the CLO/MD Library or select suitable materials from the [**CONNECT**](https://connect.clo-set.com/). Proper fabric application will affect texture baking results and help achieve a more realistic surface appearance. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51509243441561) ### **7\. Modifying Garments** Adjust the patterns to make sure that the garments dressed by the template avatar work smoothly in EveryWear. Please refer to the ['**Tips &Tricks**'](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/51485404185497-Tips-Ticks) and adjust the garments according to the relevant case.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for designing game-specific clothing, ensuring proper garment creation, simulation, and optimization while adhering to established guidelines and restrictions.

title: Tips & Tricks
content:
This guide provides the basic instructions required for the work, along with various examples of modifications. Please refer to the following content and apply it to your work according to each garment’s specific situation. * * * ### **Case #1. Adjusting Garment Length** Please refer to the length guidelines on the template avatar, making sure skirts sit above the knee and sleeves do not cover the back of the hand. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345796121) * * * ### **Case #2. How to illustrate Torn Areas** When illustrating torn areas using internal lines, the topology does not smoothly transition, and the appearance looks unnatural. In these cases, using textures instead of creating separate patterns is strongly recommended, as this approach achieves a more natural look and smoother topology. **[Topology Comparison: Pattern vs Texture]** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330162457) * * * ### **Case #3. Fixing Small patterns** For garments with small patterns, small patterns may disappear or result in unnatural topology across the entire garment during the optimization. Therefore, before optimization, merging small patterns into nearby larger patterns is strongly recommended. **[Topology Comparison: Before and After Merging]** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330163609) * **How to Merge Small Patterns** 1. Click on the line segments of two patterns you want to merge. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836713753) 2. Right-click and select ‘Merge.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836716057) * * * ### **Case #4. Adding Seam Taping to Skirt Hems** When the skirt pleats are heavily overlapped or touching each other, it can elevate rigging difficulty and cause the pleats to appear incorrect during specific movements. This may lead to clipping issues as the avatar moves. To resolve this, apply the ‘**Seam Taping** ’ function to Skirt hems to relax the pleats and enhance their overall silhouette. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330164377) * **How to apply ‘Seam Taping.’** 1. Click ‘**Edit Pattern** ’ to select the ‘Seam Taping’ option. 2. Check the ‘**Seam Taping** ’ option in the Property Editor. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512853117593)Apply ‘Seam Taping’ to the preferred segments. 3. Modifying the ‘Seam Taping’ Properties. * **Width (mm)** : set the thickness of the ‘Seam Taping.’ ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512853119769) * Physical Property: The higher the value for Bending, the more relaxed the pleats’ appearance becomes. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512836722457)Adjusting the value incrementally while checking the pleats’ silhouette for optimal results is recommended rather than starting with a significantly higher Bending value. * * * ### **Case #5. Pleated Skirts Optimization** Pleated garment patterns are usually formed by zigzag overlapping, which can cause some parts of the patterns to be hidden in the overlapped areas. To optimize these garments, it is recommended that the hidden parts of the patterns be deleted, as shown in the image below. * Before Pattern Adjustments ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330167193) * After Pattern Adjustments ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330169753) * * * ### **Case #6. Creating Internal Lines at Joint areas** Reference the example images of ‘avatar joint points’ to create internal lines in the appropriate areas of the garment. These internal lines help define the garment’s topology, improve the edge flow, and enable more natural movement during rigging. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330176153) * * * ### **Case #7. Differences between Physical Garments and Digital Garments** The structural patterns of physical garments and 3D digital garments can vary significantly. While maintaining the original design's essence is crucial, adjustments to detailed elements may be necessary for efficient optimization. For instance, elements like the back of a physical skirt or overlapping patterns on a blouse's sleeves often don't translate directly into digital garments. In such cases, removing unnecessary or hidden patterns is recommended to streamline the workflow. Moreover, unless the textures of the lining and outer fabric are different, the 'Thickness' option comes in handy for effectively simulating thickness, allowing you to eliminate one of the overlapping patterns. When designing digital garments, it's essential to consider the differences between physical and digital patterns to make practical modifications and optimizations. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345814041) * * * ### **Case #8. Refining Garment Silhouettes** When simulating with optimized polygons, you may encounter situations where the garment’s silhouette becomes awkwardly distorted. To address this, the silhouette must be refined and shaped into a more natural form. This process may also involve adjusting the positions of misaligned buttons or trims, resulting in high-quality garments. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345816729)<Before/After Comparison Image: Garment Button Position Adjustment after Mesh Optimization.> Garments are typically designed in an A-pose, with the arms extended outward. However, characters usually assume a standing pose with lowered arms in games. Adjustments should be made before rigging to ensure the garment’s wrinkles appear natural in this standing pose. For instance, wrinkles that occur only in the **A-pose** , such as those at the shoulders of a trench coat, may look unnatural in the standing pose. It is recommended that such wrinkles be removed or smoothed out to maintain a consistent and polished appearance during gameplay. Various methods exist to modify wrinkles, and designers can select the best approach to suit their workflow. The primary goal is to elevate the garment’s quality before rigging, achieving a natural silhouette that integrates seamlessly with the character’s poses. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330185369)<Before/After Comparison Image: Shoulder Wrinkle Adjustment> * * * ### **Case #9. Approaching Garment adjustment based on Avatar Mesh Handling** The process and priorities for modifying digital garments can vary depending on how the avatar mesh is processed. If the avatar mesh is deleted, there is less concern about it protruding through the garment during rigging test motions. However, greater focus is needed to ensure the garment’s overall silhouette remains clean and accurate to the intended design. For instance, if parts of the avatar mesh are visible through the garment, but the silhouette looks natural, and the design intent is well-preserved, modifications might not be necessary. However, adjustments are essential if the silhouette looks indented or distorted, regardless of whether mesh penetrations are present. When the avatar mesh is not deleted, the primary goal is to prevent it from protruding through the garment during rigging tests. After addressing this, further refinements are recommended to maintain a natural silhouette that aligns with the intended design. Defining clear workflows and inspection criteria based on how the avatar mesh is processed can enhance efficiency while maintaining high garment quality. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330187929)<Example images of acceptable garment penetrations when deleting an avatar mesh.> * * * ### **Case #10. Considerations for Button and Trim Optimization** Switching the ‘**Polygon Optimization** ’ type to ‘**Billboard** ’ can be highly beneficial when optimizing the garment accessories such as buttons, trims, and zippers. However, it's crucial to approach this change with care, considering each element's position and purpose. It is generally recommended that garment accessories be used with ‘**Mesh** ’ instead of ‘**Billboard** ’ to better preserve their shape and volume. Accessories worn near the face are especially important, as they often appear in close-up shots and can impact the overall quality. In such cases, working in ‘**Mesh** ’ is required to ensure the shape is not overly distorted. Furthermore, when an accessory plays a significant or defining role in the outfit, it’s recommended to use ‘**Mesh** ’ instead of ‘**Billboard** ’ to preserve its details. On the other hand, switching to ‘**Billboard** ’ can help optimize polygon usage effectively for less visible elements like zipper stoppers or small accessories. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345821849) * * * ### **Case #11. Capping Openings with Pattern Thickness** Openings in a garment are normally sealed with the **Auto Seal** tool, but in certain situations you can achieve the same result by extending the pattern’s **Thickness** instead. Using **Auto Seal** adds internal faces along the new cap, which raises both the polygon count and the overall complexity of the garment’s topology. By contrast, sealing a hole with **Thickness** introduces no extra internal faces, allowing you to preserve the existing polygon budget and mesh layout. Because a Thickness cap leaves no gap between the garment and the avatar, there is little space for ambient‑occlusion shadows to form; the surface can appear flat or even slightly unnatural. For that reason, this method is best reserved for tight‑fitting areas—such as sleeve cuffs or hems—where the garment already sits flush against the body. In these zones the added thickness remains virtually invisible, so you can maintain a clean silhouette while still benefiting from the lighter topology. When sealing holes with Thickness, set the **Extrusion Direction** to **Back** to keep the outer silhouette intact, and apply only as much thickness as needed to cover the opening. This ensures the inside of the garment stays hidden without distorting its overall shape.
```
💡Example image of filling holes using pattern thickness
``` * Trouser hem ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512330194713) * Armhole ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345826969) * Neckline ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512345829657) ```
Using Thickness to seal openings is generally recommended for tight‑fitting areas that receive little visual attention. However, if Fill Hole is difficult to apply—such as along a complex neckline—or if increasing the polygon count is not feasible, you can seal the opening with Thickness as an exception. ``` * * * ### **Case #12. Creating Layer Offsets with Extrusion Direction** When building a garment, the pattern’s **Extrusion Direction** is set to **Back** by default so the outer silhouette remains unchanged. If you need to add a layered offset, however, you can adjust the extrusion direction to give the pattern additional depth. Using **Forward** for this purpose is not recommended, because it moves the new thickness in the opposite direction of the default Back setting; the two layers no longer meet and the garment can look visibly disconnected. To achieve a clean offset, set the extrusion direction to **Both** and fine‑tune the thickness value until the desired step is visible while the overall silhouette stays intact.
```
💡Example image showing a layer offset created with the pattern’s Extrusion Direction
``` ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446314649)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446315801)![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512430335385) * * * ### **Case #13. Creating a Natural Collar Fold Using Internal Lines and Fold Angles** As the particle distance increases, it can become difficult to maintain a balanced collar shape. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512430336537) In such cases, you can create a more natural collar form by adding internal lines to the collar pattern. As shown in the image below, insert 2–3 internal lines near the sewing line. These lines help define the garment's topology, resulting in a smoother mesh flow.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446320281) Next, assign appropriate fold angles to the added internal lines in the Property Editor. To achieve a natural folding effect, set the fold angles between **0° and 180°** , bending outward from the collar pattern. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/51512446321433) * * * ### **Case #14. Collar Adjustment and Weight Painting Guide** Please refer to this video. [**[LINK]**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/19rpYL-RegyAaqJ3zTPjdiht0FwiUC4OZ/view?usp=sharing) * **Hide Unnecessary Mesh Using the Masking Brush** * Use the Masking Brush to hide any unnecessary mesh that is protruding from the inside or intersecting with the avatar. * **Maintain Proper Distance from the Avatar** Use the Grab Brush to slightly offset the collar so it doesn’t sit too tightly against the avatar’s neck. Leave enough space to avoid mesh penetration during animation. * **Refine the Shape** If the collar shape becomes distorted after adjusting the distance, use the Grab Brush to reshape it naturally. Make sure the silhouette flows smoothly and looks clean. * **Adjust Weights** If the collar intersects or collapses when the neck rotates, use the Smooth Multiple Joint Brush or standard Weight Brush to refine the weight painting and ensure smoother deformation. * **Final Check** Apply the test animation to check if the silhouette stays clean during movement and rotation. Make sure there’s no clipping, collapsing, or sharp deformations.
content_description: This guide offers essential instructions and practical examples for optimizing garment modifications in digital fashion design, tailored to the specific needs of each item.

title: Frequently asked questions
content: **Q: Can I use LiveSync with multiple instances of CLO or Marvelous Designer, or multiple Unreal Engine instances?** A: Unfortunately LiveSync is designed to work with a single instance of CLO or Marvelous Designer along with one Unreal Editor. **Q: Can I use LiveSync and EveryWear together?** A: EveryWear and LiveSync are separate pipelines and cannot be used together. However, you can still bring garments exported with EveryWear into Unreal Engine by simply importing the FBX file. **Q: When I send garments to Unreal Engine, the looks are different. Is it possible to make them look same?** A: Due to inherent differences in rendering systems, 'similar' looks are achieved, but it is nearly impossible to achieve identical looks. If you use CLO's V-Ray renderer, you can use [UE5's Path Tracer](https://docs.unrealengine.com/5.3/en-US/path-tracer-in-unreal-engine/) as both utilize raytracing. **Q: Which texture maps are sent to Unreal Engine via LiveSync?** A: The following texture maps are gathered and sent to Unreal Engine: * Base color map * Normal map * Roughness map * Metallic map * Reflection map * Opacity map
content_description: This web page provides essential FAQs about using LiveSync with CLO, Marvelous Designer, and Unreal Engine, addressing compatibility, rendering differences, and texture map transfer.

title: What is LiveSync?
content: **LiveSync** is a bridge which connects CLO and Unreal Editor (CLO LiveSync), or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Editor (MD LiveSync), and aims to shorten workflows requiring rendering in Unreal Engine. This is particularly useful if your workflow involves CLO or Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, however, it is worth noting that intermediate process of using other software products may be eventually eliminated as LiveSync continues to get updated. Traditional workflows involve repetitive yet tedious and destructive process of exporting garments as desired file formats and importing the results in Unreal Engine, since users need to manually manage properties expressing realistic garments in CLO or Marvelous Designer. This is caused by limitations of using specific file formats, and you can only imagine fatigue accumulated from doing file exports, imports, and potentially redoing everything if design for garments needs to be adjusted in CLO or Marvelous Designer. By establishing a direct bridge, CLO and Marvelous Designer can communicate with Unreal Editor, **eliminating needs for file exports and imports**. LiveSync features and workflows can be found in [Using LiveSync via CLO/MD LiveSync Editor](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304301544473) and [MetaHuman workflow with LiveSync](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/45304302752537). ### Tutorials & Walkthroughs For comprehensive guidance, refer to these two tutorial videos on CLO/MD LiveSync. The first is an excellent walkthrough by **Matt Workman** (Cinematography Database) using LiveSync 2.1.0, Unreal Engine 5.6, and MetaHuman. The second is our official tutorial demonstrating the workflow for earlier versions of CLO/MD LiveSync (pre-2.0.0) and Marvelous Designer 2024.0.

title: Creating Motion (MTN) - Auto Conversion
content: **Objective** Create a Motion file (.mtn) using CLO and Marvelous Designer software. Converting and redistributing motions downloaded for free or purchased from other platforms is prohibited to protect the original creators' rights. **Please create and use a motion file (.mtn) for personal use only.** * Examples: Mixamo, DAZ 3D, Reallusion-Actorcore, Unreal Marketplace, Artstation Marketplace, Sketchfab, etc **1\. How to Create a motion file (.mtn) via auto-convert features** * Manual - Auto Convert to Avatar ([CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055227373-Automatic-Rigging-Converter)/ [Marvelous Designer](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358210639897-Auto-Convert-to-Avatar-Ver-2024-0)) * Manual - Auto Convert to Motion ([CLO](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/13249323691929-Auto-Convert-to-Motion-ver-7-1)) * **※ Note: 'Auto Convert to Motion' is currently compatible with Mixamo only.** 1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO avatar. 1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a custom avatar. **1-1. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with the CLO Avatar** When using the CLO avatar, you can skip the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' and move directly to 'Auto Convert to Motion.' 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on **File > Open > Avatar**, or click on **Avatar in the Library.** 3. Load your desired CLO Avatar. 4. From the main menu, click on **Avatar >**[**Auto Convert to Motion**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/13249323691929-Auto-Convert-to-Motion-ver-7-1) 5. Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click **'Convert'** when ready.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587110169) 6. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking **'Save'** when the auto-conversion is finished.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775618995097) **※ Note: If you changed the CLO avatar's body shape, please save the avatar size file (.avs) in advance so you can easily match the size of the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' to your avatar.** **![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775578625817)** **1-2. Creating a Motion file (.mtn) compatible with a Custom Avatar** When using a custom avatar, you must run the "Auto Convert to Avatar" before applying any motion files (.mtn). 1. Launch CLO or Marvelous Designer. 2. From the main menu, click on **Avatar > **[**Auto Convert to Avatar**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055227373-Automatic-Rigging-Converter)**![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587633433)** 3. Set the options and adjust the dummy CLO avatar's body shape using Avatar Editor while the 'Auto Convert to Avatar' is on. (Click the [**LINK**](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=ZgcPIf0LqoSbaDQN&t=1746) to check the tutorial.) 4. From the main menu, click on **Avatar >**[**Auto Convert to Motion**](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/13249323691929-Auto-Convert-to-Motion-ver-7-1) 5. Select the gender and the motion file (.fbx) you have created or downloaded. Click 'Convert' when ready.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775587110169) 6. Save the motion file (.mtn) by clicking **'Save'** when the auto-conversion is finished.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775618995097) **※ Note: Please adjust the dummy CLO avatar displayed during 'Auto Convert to Motion' using the Avatar Editor to match your custom avatar's body shape.** **2\. Create a Thumbnail Image** You can upload a thumbnail for the motion file in an image or an animation. If you are creating the thumbnail as an animation, please use approximately **100 to 200 frames** from the entire motion sequence for the thumbnail. **※ Tip** : you can make the motion thumbnail longer as long as GIF/WebP animations don't exceed **50 megapixels** (the sum of sizes of all frames). Please refer to the following [website](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/transform-images/). 1. Activate **'Quality Render (3D window).'** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775636649881) 2. Check **'Show 3D Shadow'** under Environment Display. 3. Check off '**Show Ground Grid** ' under Environment Display.![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775579226649) 4. Right-click on the **3D window,** go to **Format 3D background > Solid Color**, and set the background color to #1A1A1F. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775572715673) 5. Change the mode to **'Animation'** at the top-right corner. 6. From the main menu, **File > Video Capture > Record Animation**. 7. Set the Orientation to **'Portrait'** and the resolution to **750 x 1000 pixels**. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775636989849) 8. Start recording the animation. ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775604823577) 9. Convert the animation sequence (.mp4) to webp format. * webp conversion website ([Link #1](https://mconverter.eu/convert/mp4/webp/), [Link #2](https://www.mp4.to/webp/)) **3\. CONNECT UPLOAD - Entering Asset Description** **When uploading the motion file**(.mtn)**to CONNECT, please provide detailed information about the asset for the convenience of customers.** **If detailed information is missing, asset registration may be rejected during the item approval process.** ![](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/article_attachments/45775637315225) **1\. UPLOAD (Mandatory)** Confirm the uploaded asset name and format and replace the file by pressing the **REUPLOAD** button if necessary. **2\. TITLE (****Mandatory****)** Please enter the asset name that will be displayed on CONNECT. By default, the uploaded asset's name will be set automatically as the DEFAULT TITLE. **3.****DESCRIPTION** please provide the duration of the motion file (.mtn) and specify the Avatar file (AVT) that is compatible with the motion file (.mtn) in the Description. ( **When uploading a file, if you have selected "Others" under SET AVATAR CATEGORIES > Compatibility, please provide the name and link of the avatar file (.avt) that is compatible with the motion file (.mtn). )** **4\. TAGS** **'TAGS'** is a target keyword that helps customers search and amplify your content's reach. Entering the type of assets for sale will help customers when searching for the items. **5\. ATTACHMENT** You can attach files relating to the motion file (.mtn). However, it is impossible to track attachment files attached to **'ATTACHMENT'** are being used. **6\. ADD SUB-IMAGES** You can additionally add images that highlight the characteristics of the motion file (.mtn). **7\. THUMBNAIL** Register a motion thumbnail that showcases the motion file's characteristics (.mtn). If you applied a material that is visible only in the render, please add the rendered sub-images. Registering the images where items are not visible or images unrelated to the item may lead to rejection during the item approval process.
